The adjudication that put this on onAbilityCast logged its own reason as an enum gap ('onEcho does not exist in the trigger enum - logged as a required enum addition'), and onAbilityCast is materially wrong, not merely coarse: every cast grants a stack under it, while the real gate is echoChance x a hit landing, which is exactly what damaruRhythm's kit gate exists to model. BOTH trigger positions move - the gainTriggers AND the perStackEffect's own trigger - because leaving the row on onAbilityCast would keep telling a consumer that a cast grants Rhythm, which is the bug. The 5-stack Harmonized thresholdEffect keeps trigger 'always': it is a state, not an event. The uptime NUMBERS do not change; the ('damaru', 'onAbilityCast', 'rhythm') prior in build_tables.py is re-keyed to ('damaru', 'onEcho', 'rhythm') and its authored prose already describes echo semantics ('Rhythm stacks come from ECHO procs'), so the row was always about this trigger and was merely filed under the proxy.

abilities.note: six-entry rank arrays (flags.rankZeroIncluded) already have the unranked index 0 dropped; alternate forms keep their <slot>b/<slot>c keys

uniqueGroups.policy: Non-stacking families are sourced from parsed passive prose ONLY. kb.json tags are never consulted (recon: they invent memberships). A group is `verified` only when a member's own prose states the restriction; everything else ships as `candidate` with enforcement 'none' so it is visible but inert.

constraintTags.policy: P-1 ruling: 'Tags cannot back constraints.' Every membership below cites the numeric field that proves it - a stat channel in items-stats.stats or an effect in passives-final (top-level or inside stackRule). kb.json is never read. Aura is the one tag with no numeric channel; its proof is the item's own quoted passive prose, and the rule that admits it is stated explicitly.

pen.definition: Item reduces the target's effective protections before mitigation.

antiheal.definition: Item applies Healing Reduction to enemy gods.

crit.definition: Item grants critical strike chance, or modifies critical strike damage.

aura.definition: Item applies a PERSISTENT radius effect to somebody other than the owner: a standing buff to allies in range, or a standing debuff/damage field on enemies in range.

semantics.twoReadings: passives-final stores TWO different quantities in one `uptime` field, and this table keeps both but labels them. (A) For effects under `effects`, uptime = expected fraction of the RELEVANT window during which the condition holds. (B) For effects under `stackRule.perStackEffects`, uptime = expected fraction of maxStacks the holder actually carries during that window (a stack-realization rate) - multiply by maxStacks to get expected stacks, do NOT also multiply the per-stack value by a duty cycle. Each entry's `uptimeKind` says which.
semantics.relevantWindow: combat time for defensive/self conditions; damage-dealt for offensive procs; the enemy's healing window for anti-heal; farm time for farm-stackers.
semantics.confidence: Every value is an estimate; none is game-measured. They are printed in the receipt (generator-plan: 'role-conditioned uptimes, printed in the receipt') and every receipt that touches one inherits at best a 'modeled' badge, never 'exact'.
semantics.kitGates: Four entries are gated on the GOD'S KIT, not on role: daybreak-gavel and vital-amplifier need a healing ability; stone-of-binding needs hard CC; damaru needs echo procs. The role prior is a fallback - P2 must hard-zero these for gods whose kit cannot trigger them, or the search will buy them for gods that get nothing.

hooks.contract: This is the P1 REGISTRY, not the implementation. Each entry names a hook the TS engine must expose in P2 and pins the EXACT prose that hook has to reproduce. The prose is the spec: if an implementation cannot be read back off the quoted line, it is wrong. `passBHookNames` records what the second independent normalization pass wanted to call the same item's hooks - useful when a P2 implementation has to decide what the hook actually does. R3 (2026-08-28): an item names `hooks: string[]`, so an item with two hooks appears under BOTH entries and `hooksOnThisItem` names its siblings; implement each entry separately and do not assume one hook owns the whole record.

chainGods.defaultPolicy: engineChain defaults to [1.0] for the 58 gods with no chain and for any variant that failed to parse. Where a chain IS known it is shipped verbatim; the P2 evaluator may use it for burst terms and MUST NOT re-apply it to sustained DPS (that would double-count, since the multipliers are already DPS-neutral).

burnDown.rule: Anything listed here needs in-game observation; everything else is wiki-exact.

open.workaround: Damage multipliers are NOT stated. The note gives the WEAPON order (Mourning, Clarent, Clarent, Mourning) and swing-time multipliers only. Mordred's two weapons carry different damage scaling on the same page (Mourning 100% STR / 20% INT / 100% AD; Clarent 60% STR / 100% INT / 60% AD), so his chain is a per-hit SCALING SWAP, not a damage multiplier. Modeled as damage [1,1,1,1] with an alternating scaling vector - the damage half is the only genuinely unknown chain number in the roster.

open.missing: how the 40%-damage / 20%-healing item-proc scaling composes with per-item on-hit effects
open.workaround: Not a chain at all: a sustained-fire basic that starts at 5 attacks/sec and decays to 2/sec, where item hit effects proc at 40% damage and 20% healing. hitsPerCast=5 is already in abilities.json from the notes. The 40%/20% proc scaling is the number that matters for item valuation and it is NOT modeled anywhere yet.

open.missing: which weapon is active during a given fight (a playstyle input, not a wiki gap)
open.workaround: Four separate chains, one per weapon, selected by the most recent ability used and persisting until 7s without dealing or taking damage. Hammer is the only chain in the entire roster whose damage and swing multipliers DIFFER (1.5/1/1.5 damage vs 1.5/1/1.25 swing), which makes it the only chain with a sustained-DPS multiplier other than 1.0 (1.0667x). Which weapon is active is a playstyle input the engine does not have; default to Greatsword and expose the others as a what-if.

legality.order: LSB-first within each 32-bit word; item i lives at words[i>>5] >> (i&31) & 1
legality.poolRule: tier-3 items of any type, plus Starter / Relic / God Specific items; Consumables, Curios and non-Starter tier-1/2 components are excluded. God-specific items are masked to their owner. No OB42 item carries a role restriction, so role enters the mask only through the god's per-role STR/INT scaling family (ItemStore.Filter.Role.<Role>.<STR|INT>).
legality.familyExclusionRule: RS52: the STR/INT exclusion is DROPPED for any (god, role) pair whose own curated build holds an item of the excluded family - the curated build is the evidence that the role's scaling-family tag is wrong for that pair. Per-pair, data-driven, and gated: gate_curated_legality() makes any remaining contradiction a hard build failure.

goldPrices.model: non-negative least squares, no intercept: totalcost ~ sum_c price_c * stat_c
goldPrices.collinearityGuard: channels with fewer than 3 independent nonzero observations across the T3 corpus are dropped

conditionNumber.note: the ill-conditioning verdict reads the column-normalized number; the raw one is dominated by unit scale

goldPrices.note: Regression accepted. The raw condition number is a unit-scale artifact (health ~500 vs critChance ~0.2); the column-normalized number is the one that measures collinearity.
goldPrices.unitConvention: ALL percent-family channels are stored as fractions (0.20 = 20%), so their price is gold per 1.00 = per 100 percentage points. The full list is attackSpeedPct, critChance, critDamageBonus, lifestealPct, cooldownRate, moveSpeed, pathfinding, penPct, plating, dampening, echoChance, tenacity, healingReduction. Every other channel (strength, intelligence, attackDamage, health, mana, manaRegen, hp5, mp5, physProt, magProt, penFlat, adaptiveStr, adaptiveInt) is a flat point value. Corrected 2026-08-28: moveSpeed was missing from this list, and plating/dampening/tenacity used to ship raw percent POINTS on the item side while the passive layer shipped fractions for the same channel.

goldCurve.method: median cumulative itemTotalCost at each held-item count k, over every curated build of that role with at least k items. Median = mean of the two middle samples on an even count. Variable-length aware: n shrinks with k and is published per slot; a slot whose coverage falls below 30% of the role's builds is not published. A running max keeps the curve non-decreasing (flagged monotoneRaised, raw value kept).
goldCurve.unit: gold (itemTotalCost), BEFORE the search's GOLD_BUDGET_SLACK multiplier - the slack is a search prior and lives in src/search/context.ts, not in the data
goldCurve.supersedes: the per-request reference build's own cumulative cost (P3-VERIFIER-REPORT.md V1 root cause)
